section_summary: This section contains wartime activity reports on Filipinos in Shanghai, compiled mainly from signed statements taken in October and November 1945. The reports examine the Japanese sponsored Filipino Association, allegiance to the wartime Philippine government, benefit performances for Japanese forces, and allegations that some Filipinos informed on others. Several subjects dispute the allegations or describe pressure to cooperate.

subfiles.title: A. Y. Celis
subfiles.about: Statements and documentary extracts assess Celis's wartime activities in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The continuation gathers allegations that Celis organized pro-Japanese Filipino meetings and concerts, encouraged allegiance to the wartime Philippine government, and had contact with Japanese police. It includes conflicting testimony about an alleged informant list and extracts from association records and resolutions bearing his signature.

subfiles.title: Vedasto Conde
subfiles.about: Statements describe Conde's Japanese contacts, trading, and interpreting for Conrado Uy.
subfiles.summary: Evangelista alleges Conde traded controlled goods and was a Japanese informer; Gonzaga says Conde interpreted for Uy on an inland tour.

subfiles.title: Buenaventura Constantino
subfiles.about: Witness accounts and association records examine Constantino's wartime conduct.
subfiles.summary: Constantino acknowledges visiting the Japanese Consulate and repeating warnings about Filipinos who refused allegiance. Other witnesses accuse him of promoting Japanese benefit concerts, threatening dissenters, helping bring about an arrest, and accepting a relief committee post. The report also records his signatures on association material and his response to some allegations.

subfiles.title: Jose Contreras
subfiles.about: Contreras's statements, a memorandum, and witness testimony address his leadership of Shanghai's Filipino community.
subfiles.summary: Contreras describes his wartime concerts, allegiance registration work, association leadership, and dealings with Japanese officials while arguing that he tried to protect the community. Witnesses instead describe coercion of musicians, pro-Japanese speeches, threats, and possible involvement in arrests. The report compares those accounts with association documents, petitions, and photographs.

subfiles.title: Terso Cruz
subfiles.about: Statements concern Cruz's signing of an accusation during a Japanese interrogation.
subfiles.summary: Cruz says he signed a paper accusing Evangelista after being told it could secure his cousin's release. Other statements describe the resulting allegations, allegiance registration, and his signatures on Filipino Association records.

subfiles.title: W. Cruz
subfiles.about: Cruz explains his allegiance vote and petition signatures; Evangelista alleges broader cooperation.
subfiles.summary: Cruz attributes his “yes” vote to fear of Japanese discovery of pistol bullets. Evangelista alleges he supported Japanese forces and joined wartime ceremonies; the report notes his petition signatures.

subfiles.title: I. Dizon
subfiles.about: Dizon describes the Filipino Association's formation and denies political involvement.
subfiles.summary: Dizon says threats shaped membership and leadership elections. Other witnesses allege he supported Contreras and Japanese benefit events; the report records his association and petition signatures.

subfiles.title: Ricardo B. Dizon
subfiles.about: Dizon reports on Filipino leaders and explains his concert participation.
subfiles.summary: Dizon describes pro-Japanese statements and pressure from Alindada, Uy, and others, and says he played at two concerts under pressure. Evangelista disputes his account of his role; the report records Dizon's petition and association signatures.

subfiles.title: Alfredo Figueroa
subfiles.about: Figueroa explains his allegiance vote and a list of names on a music sheet.
subfiles.summary: Figueroa says concern for his Japanese wife and children led him to vote “yes.” Evangelista alleges active collaboration, while a note treats Figueroa's disparaging list of Filipinos as apparently nonpolitical.

subfiles.title: Amado C. Francia
subfiles.about: Brief biographical note on musician Amado C. Francia's broadcasts and performances in Tianjin.
subfiles.summary: An informer says Francia worked for Japanese broadcasts and military relief under pressure from Cadz and Williams.

subfiles.title: L. Gonzaga
subfiles.about: Gonzaga denies informing for Japan; former prisoners allege he betrayed them.
subfiles.summary: Gonzaga says he documented collaborators and assisted Dasmarinas out of sympathy. Evangelista and Espino allege he passed information to Japanese authorities; the report notes his submitted record book.

subfiles.title: A. Herrera
subfiles.about: Report on deceased association treasurer Herrera's wartime signatures and activities.
subfiles.summary: The report records Herrera's association signatures, allegiance vote, and independence parade participation; Evangelista adds allegations of benefit performances.
